gaps.concept: Acute HIV infection causes fever, rash, pharyngitis, and generalized lymphadenopathy within weeks of exposure, often before antibody tests become positive.
gaps.why_tested: A mononucleosis-like illness after sexual exposure prompts HIV RNA testing despite negative antibody results.

gaps.concept: AIDS is defined by CD4 count below 200 cells/mm³ or an AIDS-defining illness; progressive CD4 loss causes cellular immunodeficiency.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks whether a CD4 count or associated illness establishes progression to AIDS.

gaps.concept: HIV viral load measures replication and treatment response; CD4 count measures immune function.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks which laboratory measure tracks ART efficacy versus risk from immunodeficiency.

gaps.concept: Infants with perinatal HIV exposure require HIV RNA or DNA testing because transferred maternal antibodies make antibody tests unreliable.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn has a positive HIV antibody test, and the stem asks how infection is established.

gaps.concept: Early HIV strains commonly use CCR5 and infect macrophages; later CXCR4-using strains preferentially infect T cells.
gaps.why_tested: A stem links disease stage or cell tropism to the HIV coreceptor used.

gaps.concept: Homozygous CCR5-Δ32 reduces susceptibility to CCR5-tropic HIV.
gaps.why_tested: An exposed person remains uninfected, and a coreceptor deletion explains the finding.

gaps.concept: HIV Nef reduces surface MHC class I expression, impairing cytotoxic T-cell recognition.
gaps.why_tested: A viral protein is identified from its immune-evasion effect.

gaps.concept: NRTIs require intracellular phosphorylation and terminate viral DNA chains; NNRTIs inhibit reverse transcriptase allosterically without phosphorylation.
gaps.why_tested: A drug mechanism stem distinguishes two reverse transcriptase inhibitor classes.

gaps.concept: HIV protease inhibitors prevent cleavage of viral polyproteins, producing immature, noninfectious virions; integrase inhibitors block insertion of viral DNA.
gaps.why_tested: A replication-stage diagram asks where an ART class acts.

gaps.concept: NRTI inhibition of mitochondrial DNA polymerase γ can cause lactic acidosis and hepatic steatosis.
gaps.why_tested: An ART recipient develops metabolic acidosis and fatty liver, prompting identification of the drug class.

gaps.concept: Didanosine and stavudine can cause pancreatitis and peripheral neuropathy through mitochondrial toxicity.
gaps.why_tested: An older antiretroviral regimen is linked to pancreatic or neurologic adverse effects.

gaps.concept: Indinavir can cause nephrolithiasis.
gaps.why_tested: Renal colic develops after starting a protease inhibitor.

gaps.concept: ART uses multiple active drugs to suppress replication and limit selection of resistant HIV variants.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks why single-agent HIV therapy rapidly fails.

gaps.concept: Genital HSV-2 recurs and sheds asymptomatically more often than genital HSV-1; either type can cause genital disease.
gaps.why_tested: A recurrent genital-lesion stem asks which HSV type is more likely or how types differ.

gaps.concept: Genital HSV can spread during asymptomatic shedding; suppressive antiviral therapy reduces recurrences and transmission.
gaps.why_tested: Transmission occurs from a partner without visible lesions.

gaps.concept: Primary genital HSV may cause fever, dysuria, and tender inguinal nodes; recurrences are usually milder and may follow a tingling prodrome.
gaps.why_tested: A stem distinguishes a first episode from recurrent genital herpes.

gaps.concept: New maternal genital HSV infection near delivery poses greater neonatal risk than recurrent infection; active lesions at labor favor cesarean delivery.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnancy vignette asks which maternal infection presents the highest transmission risk or indicates delivery precautions.

gaps.concept: Type-specific HSV serology can aid diagnosis when lesions are absent; lesion PCR is preferred when lesions are present.
gaps.why_tested: A patient reports recurrent ulcers but has no lesion available for PCR.

gaps.concept: Foscarnet directly inhibits viral DNA polymerase without thymidine-kinase activation and can cause nephrotoxicity.
gaps.why_tested: Thymidine-kinase-deficient, acyclovir-resistant HSV requires an alternative antiviral.

gaps.concept: Oncogenic HPV E6 promotes p53 degradation, while E7 inactivates Rb, releasing cell-cycle inhibition.
gaps.why_tested: A cervical dysplasia or cancer stem asks which tumor suppressors viral proteins disable.

gaps.concept: High-risk HPV DNA may integrate into the host genome; disruption of E2 increases E6 and E7 expression.
gaps.why_tested: A stem links persistent HPV infection to malignant transformation.

gaps.concept: Koilocytes show perinuclear halos and enlarged, irregular hyperchromatic nuclei on cervical cytology or wart histology.
gaps.why_tested: A Pap smear or biopsy image asks for the causative virus.

gaps.concept: Condyloma acuminata are exophytic, cauliflower-like anogenital warts; syphilitic condyloma lata are broad, flat, moist plaques.
gaps.why_tested: An anogenital-lesion stem asks the learner to distinguish HPV from secondary syphilis.

gaps.concept: HPV-related cervical dysplasia arises mainly at the squamocolumnar transformation zone; persistent high-risk infection can progress to invasive carcinoma.
gaps.why_tested: A biopsy-site or dysplasia-progression stem asks where HPV-associated cervical disease begins.

gaps.concept: Cervical cytology and high-risk HPV DNA testing detect precancer risk; HPV testing does not diagnose visible genital warts.
gaps.why_tested: A screening or diagnostic-test question contrasts cervical precancer with condyloma acuminata.

gaps.concept: HIV-associated immunosuppression increases HPV persistence, recurrent warts, and cervical or anal precancer and cancer risk.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with HIV has persistent HPV or a screening question asks why risk is elevated.

gaps.concept: The nine-valent HPV vaccine contains noninfectious L1 virus-like particles and prevents targeted infections best before exposure; it does not treat existing lesions.
gaps.why_tested: A vaccine-mechanism stem asks whether vaccination contains live virus or clears established warts.

gaps.concept: Podofilox disrupts microtubules in genital warts and should be avoided during pregnancy.
gaps.why_tested: A wart-treatment mechanism or pregnancy contraindication stem names podofilox.

gaps.concept: Genital HPV spreads through skin contact, including areas condoms do not cover.
gaps.why_tested: A prevention stem asks why barrier use reduces but does not eliminate HPV transmission.

gaps.concept: Molluscum poxvirus replicates in the cytoplasm; genital lesions can spread through sexual skin contact, fomites, or autoinoculation.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks for the unusual replication site or how umbilicated genital papules spread.

gaps.concept: Molluscum is usually self-limited in immunocompetent patients; persistent genital lesions may be treated with lesion-directed methods such as cryotherapy or curettage.
gaps.why_tested: A vignette contrasts the expected course in a healthy patient with treatment of persistent genital lesions.
